A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same contextual anomaly-detection framework and CWAE experiments despite the changed title. Text, equations, figures and tables are readable, including v2's added Appendix A; v1 has no appendix.

before.justification: Sections 6–7 report original experiments on eight datasets, including benchmark comparisons, context selection and analyses across conditional model architectures.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results and adds approximate training, inference and context-selection timings in Appendix A.8.

M1.justification: The CWAE architecture, reconstruction-plus-MMD objective, one-epoch joint-validation-loss context selection and context-normalized anomaly scoring are retained. Appendix A supplies implementation details without establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate bank, beth, census, cmc, kdd, lanl, sf and spotify with identical dataset statistics. No additional domain, task or test scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain DSVDD, RDP, RCA, ICL, DIF, SLAD, DTE and WAE. Section 7.3 retains the same CWAE, CVAE, CMDN and CADI comparisons against their non-contextual counterparts.

E3.justification: Appendix A.6.3 expands the stated evaluation prescription beyond AUCROC and rank to AUC-PR and precision, recall and F1 at the test-set F1-maximizing threshold. No corresponding additional scores are reported, and the original AUCROC protocol remains unchanged. Newly disclosed split and training settings do not establish that the benchmark experiments changed or were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix A.8 adds computational-cost analysis through dataset-specific timing estimates and context-search cost calculations. The existing threshold visualization, optimal-context analysis and cross-architecture analysis in Section 7 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 6 and Appendix A.5.5 newly disclose a fixed random seed of 43. This does not establish additional runs; neither version reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 have identical numerical entries, and the existing plotted results and cross-architecture gains are retained. New numerical reporting concerns runtime: Table 8 gives approximate CWAE training times from two minutes to 1.5 hours, while A.8 adds inference and context-selection estimates.

T1.justification: The conditional anomaly-detection definitions, variance decomposition and generative-versus-discriminative reasoning are retained. Appendix equations spell out existing likelihood conversion, losses and selection criteria rather than introducing a new theorem, proof or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that conditional modeling, automatic context selection and the CWAE instantiation improve tabular anomaly detection. v2 foregrounds the general framework and theoretical motivation, but these contributions and their scientific scope were already present in v1.

C2.justification: Sections 3.1 and 5.3 add substantive explanations for single-feature conditioning, mostly-normal validation data and potentially less reliable proxy validation. v2 removes Section 9's discussion of context-dependent fairness benefits, bias risks and explainability costs. The existing threshold-comparability limitation remains.

D1.justification: New Appendix A substantially expands reproducibility information: embedding and layer dimensions, regularization and comparator configurations, optimizer and training settings, approximately 60/20/20 fixed splits, unknown-category handling, a ten-batch validation limit, and hardware/software specifications. These are primarily newly documented details of retained experiments, not demonstrated implementation changes.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive distinctions from prior methods are retained: tabular data without predefined context, lightweight conditional modeling and automatic context selection. Bibliographic formatting and the stronger emphasis on a unified framework do not establish a changed relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, contribution list and conclusion receive targeted rewrites emphasizing contextual learning, with expanded explanations in Sections 3.1 and 5.3. The ethics section is removed and an implementation appendix added, while most main-text wording and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: The document changes from a compact two-column layout to a single-column format with substantially different author presentation, typography, captions and figure/table placement. All four figure images are reused and resized; new Tables 6–8 present hyperparameters, software dependencies and runtime estimates.

improvement.justification: Appendix A addresses v1's sparse reproducibility documentation with concrete architecture, training, split, seed and hardware information, while the expanded explanations clarify practical assumptions. These gains are tempered by removal of the context-specific fairness and explainability discussion and ambiguities in the appendix, including CMDN's Gaussian-mixture likelihood versus its later cross-entropy scoring description.
